echinate: pollen wall with echini longer and/or wider than 1 µm
apertures sunken: characteristic shape of pollen grains in dry condition as a consequence of harmomegathy
sexine: term used for light microscopy, describing the structured/sculptured outer layer of the exine
intine: part of the pollen wall next to the cytoplasm, mainly consisting of polysaccharides; the intine can be monolayered or bilayered; see also “ektintine” and “endintine”
shape: 3-dimensional form of a pollen grain in relation to the P/E-ratio
outline quadrangular: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
outline circular: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
tetrad decussate: unit of 4 pollen grains arranged in 2 pairs in 2 different plains
clypeate: pollen with exine subdivided into shields
bireticulate: reticulate ornamentation, where the lumina of the coarse-meshed reticulum are filled by a fine-meshed reticulum
tetrad planar: unit of 4 pollen grains arranged in one plane; can be: tetragonal, T-shaped, linear
croton pattern: special type of reticulum cristatum formed by regularly arranged suprasculpture elements on muri
endexine compact-continuous: distinct exine layer between ektexine and intine; endexine can be compact, spongy or lamellar as well as continuous, discontinuous, absent, or in aperture only
ektintine: the outer layer of the intine which is adjacent to the exine
monosaccate: pollen grain with a single saccus
polyad: unit of more than 4 pollen grains (multiple of 4)
pollenkitt: pollen coating consisting of sticky substances, mainly lipids
pollen coating: general term applied to organic compounds usually produced by the tapetum, located on the exine and/ or in exine cavities; see also: pollenkitt, tryphine, primexine matrix
micro-: prefix for small; features between 1-0,5 µm: microbaculate, microclavate, microechinate, microgemmate, microrugulate, microreticulate, microverrucate; not used in combination with striate and foveolate
heterobrochate: reticulate pollen wall with lumina of different sizes
semitectate: pollen grain with a discontinuous tectum
aperture: a region of the pollen wall that differs significantly from its surroundings in morphology and/or anatomy, presumed to function usually as germination site and to play a role in harmomegathy
tetrad tetrahedral: unit of 4 pollen grains in which the centers of the grains define a tetrahedron
scabrate: term used for light microscopy only, describing minute sculpture elements of undefined shape and of a size close to the resolution limit of the light microscope
free-standing columellae: columellae not covered by a tectum in semitectate pollen grains
outline polygonal: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
infoldings: consequence of harmomegathy in dry condition, e.g., boat-shaped, cup-shaped, irregularly infolded
spiraperturate: pollen grain with one or more spiral aperture(s)
annulate: pollen grain with an annulus or annuli
interapertural area sunken: characteristic shape of pollen grains in dry condition as a consequence of harmomegathy
endintine: inner layer of the intine which is adjacent to the ­cytoplasm
planaperturate: pollen grain with an angular outline, where the apertures are situated between the angles
isodiametric: pollen grain with a polar axis equal to the equatorial diameter
ring-like aperture: circumferential aperture (situated more or less equatorially or, rarely, meridionally)
infratectum granular: layer between tectum and foot layer or endexine (if foot layer is absent); infratectum can be alveolate, columellate, granular or absent
viscin thread: acetolysis resistant thread arising from the exine
outline triangular: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
synaperturate: pollen grain with anastomosing apertures: syncolpate, syncolporate
acalymmate: dyads, tetrads, and polyads covered by an exine envelope which is discontinuous at the junctions between the monads
boat-shaped: characteristic shape of sulcate pollen grains in dry condition as a consequence of harmomegathy
pollen class: artificial grouping of pollen grains that share one or more distinctive characters
suprasculpture: secondary sculpture elements positioned on the primary sculpture of the pollen surface
nano-: prefix for very small, features between 0.50.1 µm: nanobaculate, nanoclavate, nanoechinate, nanogemmate, nanorugulate, nanoreticulate, nanoverrucate; not used in combination with striate and foveolate
monad: unit consisting of a single pollen grain
nexine: term used for light microscopy, describing the inner, unstructured layer of the exine
heteropolar: pollen grain with different proximal and distal faces
aperture membrane: exine layer covering an aperture; aperture membrane (colpus or porus membrane) can be psilate or ornamented
supratectal element: sculpture element positioned on top of the tectum
angulaperturate: pollen grain with an angular outline where the ­apertures are located at the angles
pseudomonad: unit of a permanent tetrad with 3 rudimentary pollen grains
pantoaperturate: pollen grain with apertures distributed more or less regularly over the surface: pantocolpate, pantocolporate, pantoporate
ektoaperture: outer part of a compound aperture
endoaperture: inner part of a compound aperture
prolate: pollen grain with a polar axis longer than the equatorial diameter
heteroaperturate: pollen grain with different types of apertures; only one type presumed to function as germination site; see: pseudocolpus
outline elliptic: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
striato-reticulate: ornamentation intermediate between striate and reticulate
saccate: pollen grain with one or more air sacs
outline lobate: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
reticulum cristatum: special type of reticulum; muri with prominent suprasculpture
baculate: pollen wall with bacula longer and/or wider than 1 µm
cup-shaped: characteristic shape of pollen grains in dry condition as a consequence of harmomegathy
eutectate: pollen grain with a predominantly continuous tectum
homobrochate: reticulate pollen wall with lumina of uniform size
gemmate: pollen wall with gemmae larger than 1 µm in diameter
oblate: pollen grain with a polar axis shorter than the equatorial diameter
aperturate: pollen grain with one or more apertures
clavate: pollen wall with clavae longer and/or wider than 1 µm
lophate: pollen wall with coarse meshed pattern formed by lophae and lacunae
isopolar: pollen grain with identical proximal and distal faces
bridge: exine connection(s) between the margins of an ­aperture
infratectum columellate: layer between tectum and foot layer or endexine (if foot layer is absent); infratectum can be alveolate, columellate, granular or absent
stephanoaperturate: apertures situated at the equator (term usually used for 6 or more apertures); see also: stephanocolpate, stephanocolporate, stephanoporate
acetolysis: widely used technique for preparing pollen and spores especially for light microscopy
actuopalynology: the study of pollen and spores of extant plants
aeropalynology: the study of palynomorphs found in the atmosphere
alveolate: infratectum with compartments of irregular size and shape
alveolus (lat., pl. alveoli): compartment(s) of irregular size and shape
annulus (lat. pl. annuli): ring like wall thickening surrounding a porus or ulcus
apex (lat., pl. apices): applied to outermost tips in the equatorial plane of pollen
atrium (lat., pl. atria): space between diverging exine layers within the aperture
brevicolporus (lat., pl. brevicolpori): short colpus in a compound aperture situated ­equatorially
brochus (lat., pl. brochi): mesh of a reticulum consisting of one lumen and the adjoining half of the muri
calymmate: dyads, tetrads, and polyads covered by a continuous exine envelope
cappa (lat., pl. cappae): the thick-walled proximal face of the corpus in a ­saccate pollen grain
cavea (lat., pl. caveae): cavity between the sexine and nexine in the interapertural area
colporoidate: used for light microscopy only, describing compound apertures composed of a colpus (ektoaperture) with an indistinct endoaperture
colporus (lat., pl. colpori): compound aperture composed of a colpus (ektoaperture) combined with an endoaperture of variable size and shape
colpus (lat., pl. colpi): elongated aperture (length/width ratio > 2) situated at the equator or globally distributed
columella (lat., pl. columellae): rod-like structure element, supporting a tectum
compound aperture: aperture with two or more components that are situated in more than one wall layer, e.g., colporus
copropalynology: the study of palynomorphs in coprolites or feces
corpus (lat., pl. corpora): body of a saccate pollen grain
costa (lat., pl. costae): thickening of the nexine/endexine bordering an endoaperture
cryopalynology: the study of palynomorphs found in ice
diaperturate: pollen grain with two apertures: disulcate, dicolpate, dicolporate, diporate
dispersal unit: unit in which pollen is dispersed (e.g., monad, tetrad, pollinarium)
distal: directing away from the center of a tetrad (deduced from tetrad stage)
elastoviscin: highly elastic, not acetolysis resistant substance in Orchidaceae, which interconnects the subunits (monads, tetrads, or massulae) of a pollinium and builds up the caudicles
endexine: distinct exine layer between ektexine and intine; endexine can be compact, spongy or lamellar as well as continuous, discontinuous, absent, or in aperture only
endoplica: fold of the inner exine layer
equator: imaginary line encircling a pollen grain between the proximal and distal poles
equatorial: preposition indicating a region on the pollen surface
equatorial diameter: diameter of a pollen grain at the equator
equatorial plane: imaginary plane at the equator, perpendicular to the polar axis
equatorial view: view of a pollen grain where the equator is directed towards the observer
eurypalynous: plant taxa characterized by a significant variation in pollen morphology
exine: outer layer of the pollen wall, usually resistant to ­acetolysis
fischer's law: refers to the most frequent aperture arrangement where a pair of apertures occur at six points in a tetrad
rule: refers to the most frequent aperture arrangement where a pair of apertures occur at six points in a tetrad
foot layer: inner layer of an ektexine that can be continuous, ­discontinuous, perforated or absent
forensic palynology: the study of palynomorphs found in crime related samples
foveola (pl. foveolae): roundish lumen more than 1 µm in diameter; distance between two adjacent lumina larger than their ­diameter
frustrate: special mental condition of palynologists discussing terminology of pollen; see
garside's law: refers to the unusual arrangement of apertures where a group of three apertures occur at four points in a tetrad
generative cell: progenitor cell of the sperm cells
geniculum (pl. genicula): colpus buckled in the equatorial region
granular: infratectum composed of granula, cluster of granula or elements of different size and shape (never solid and rod-like)
granulum (lat., pl. granula): sculpture element of different/indefinable shape, equal or smaller than 0,1 µm in diameter (hard to outline)
harmomegathy: mechanism permitting changes in shape and size of the pollen grain due to varying hydration status
hexaaperturate: pollen grain with 6 apertures: hexacolpate, hexacolporate, hexaporate
iatropalynology: the study of palynomorphs causing allergies
impression mark: a linear or Y-shaped mark on the proximal polar area of a pollen grain retained from the tetrad stage
infratectum: layer between tectum and foot layer or endexine (if foot layer is absent); infratectum can be alveolate, columellate, granular or absent
internal tectum: additional more or less continuous layer within the infratectum
lacuna (lat., pl. lacunae): depressed area surrounded by ridges (lophae) in lophate pollen grains
laesura (lat., pl. laesurae): a single arm of a tetrad mark
leptoma (gr., pl. leptomata): thinning of the pollen wall on the distal face in conifers, presumed to function as germination area
lo-analysis: light microscopic method for analyzing pollen surfaces
lobate: outline in polar view of a pollen grain with bulged interapertural areas (mainly in dry pollen grains)
lumen (lat., pl. lumina): space enclosed by muri in reticulate pollen grains
margo (lat., pl. margines): exine area with different ornamentation bordering a colpus/colporus/sulcus
massula (lat., pl. massulae): unit of more than 4 pollen grains but less than the locular content of a theca
megaspore: the larger spore in vascular plants
melissopalynology: the study of palynomorphs found in honey
meridian: imaginary line on the pollen surface connecting proximal and distal poles
meridional: preposition indicating a direction on the pollen surface
microspore: the smaller spore of heterosporous vascular plants
muri (lat. sing. murus): ornamentation elements forming the meshes in a reticulum
nodulum (lat., pl. nodula): small body located on the nexine of the central saccus area
normapolles: group of Cretaceous and lower Paleogene pollen, usually triaperturate, with a complex pore apparatus
oblique view: view of a pollen grain neither in polar nor in equatorial view
oncus (lat., pl. onci): lens-shaped body located beneath the aperture, not resistant to acetolysis
operculum (lat., pl. opercula): distinctly delimited exine structure covering an aperture
ornamentation: applied in palynology to surface features
outline: describes the contour of pollen grains in polar and/or equatorial view, e.g., circular, elliptic, triangular, quadrangular, polygonal, irregular, lobate see also: amb
p: refers to the length of the polar axis between the two poles compared to the equatorial diameter
e-ratio: refers to the length of the polar axis between the two poles compared to the equatorial diameter
palynogram: diagram summarizing the main morphological features of a palynomorph
palynomorph: general term for all biological entities found in palynological samples, e.g., pollen, spores, cysts, diatoms
papilla (lat., pl. papillae): small protuberance typical for Taxodioideae pollen located distally
pentaaperturate: pollen grain with 5 apertures: pentacolpate, pentacolporate, pentaporate
perforate: pollen wall with holes less than 1 µm in diameter
pharmacopalynology: the study of palynomorphs in drugs
pinus subgenus strobus type: bisaccate pollen grain with hemispherical sacci
pinus subgenus pinus type: bisaccate pollen grain with balloon-like sacci
pluricolumellate: reticulate pollen wall with more than one row of columellae beneath the muri
polar area: region at and around the pole(s)
polar axis: imaginary line between the proximal and the distal pole of a pollen grain
polar view: view of a pollen grain in which the pole is directed towards the observer
polarity: orientation of the proximal and distal pole of a pollen grain resulting from tetrad stage
pole: outermost proximal and/or distal point of a pollen grain
pollen analysis: study of assemblages of dispersed palynomorphs
pollen coating vesicles: tapetum derived vesicles covering the perforated footlayer in mature pollen grains in, e.g.,
pollen grain (engl., pl. pollen grains o: the male gametophyte of seed plants; source and carrier for the male gametes (spermatozoids or sperm cells)
pollen mother cell: diploid cell forming a tetrad of four haploid microspores by meiosis
pollen tube: tube produced by the vegetative cell as part of the fertilization process (transports the male gametes)
pollen type: term categorizing pollen grains; often used in connection with a distinct taxon
pollen unit: morphological unit of mature pollen grains (e.g., monad, tetrad)
pollen wall: layer(s) enclosing the cytoplasm of a pollen grain
pollinarium (lat., pl. pollinaria): dispersal unit of pollinium (or pollinia) plus secretions and/or tissues that aid in the removal of the structure from the flower
pollination: transfer of pollen from the male to the female reproductive organs in seed plants
pollinium (lat., pl. pollinia): unit of a more or less interconnected loculiform pollen mass
polychotomosulcus: sulcus with more than three arms
pontoperculum (lat., pl. pontopercula): elongated operculum linked to the ends of the ­aperture
pororate: pollen grain with compound apertures composed of a circular “ektoporus” and “endoporus”
more or less circular aperture; pori located at the equator or regularly spread over the pollen grain
pre(prae)-pollen: microspores of certain extinct basal seed plants occurring from the Late Devonian until the Cretaceous, characterized by proximal and sometimes additional distal apertures, and presumed proximal germination
primexine: polysaccharidic layer formed during early developmental stage wherein the later exine structures are preformed
primexine matrix: pollen coatings consisting of primexine remnants in mature pollen grains
proximal: pollen face/pole/side directing towards the center of the tetrad (deduced from tetrad stage)
pseudocolpus: colpus in a heteroaperturate pollen grain, presumed not to function as germination site
reticulum (lat. pl. reticula): network like pattern consisting of muri and lumina
retipilate: reticulum formed by rows of pila instead of muri
saccus (lat., pl. sacci): exinous expansion forming an air sac
sculpture: ornamentation elements on the pollen surface, e.g., echini, bacula, clavae, verrucae
spore: general term for a reproductive unit (sexual, asexual) in plants and fungi
sporoderm: general term for the pollen/spore wall
sporopollenin: main component of the exine, consisting of acetolysisresistant biopolymers
stenopalynous: plant taxa characterized by only slight variation in pollen morphology
striae (lat., sing. stria): elongated ornamentation elements separated by grooves parallelly arranged
structure: the stratification of a pollen wall
tapetum: specialized layer of cells lining the locule and participating in the nourishment of pollen grains, wall formation, and synthesis of pollen coatings
tectum (lat., pl. tecta): outer more or less continuous ektexine layer; tectum condition can be eutectate or semitectate
tenuitas (lat., pl. tenuitates): general term for a thinning of the pollen wall
tetraaperturate: pollen grain with 4 apertures: tetracolpate, tetracolporate, tetraporate
tetrad mark: mark on the proximal face of a spore retained from the postmeiotic stage functioning as germination area (linear = monolete, y-shaped = trilete)
­treme: suffix for a germination site (aperture, laesura); for kata-, ana-, zono-, and pantotreme
triaperturate: pollen grain with 3 apertures: tricolpate, tricolporate, triporate
tryphine: pollen coating consisting mainly of lipids mixed with membrane remnants
ubisch body (engl., pl. ubisch bodies): polymorphic sporopollenin-­element produced by the tapetum
ulcus (lat., pl. ulci): more or less circular aperture located distally
vegetative cell: the larger of the two cells formed after first pollen ­mitosis
vegetative nucleus: the nucleus of the vegetative cell
